name: Msafe Equipments Ltd
title: Msafe Equipments Ltd - 544695 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Msafe's Q1 FY27 PAT rose 44% to ₹7.27 cr on rental-led growth, but the transcript is heavily garbled and capacity additions (Mathura plant targeted May 2027, Delhi premises) are delayed and not yet producing.

triggers.label: Mathura plant target slipped to May 2027
triggers.quote: we continue to target commencement of operations by May 2027

guidance.value: Not committed; initial phase may compress margins

red_flags.label: Margin guidance withdrawn; initial margins may fall

evasions.quote: How can I define the peak? Basically, it is not a mountain.

summary.headline: Msafe Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 40% YoY to ₹31.79 crore and PAT rose 44% to ₹7.27 crore, with the rental business up 24%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹31.79 crore (up 40% YoY from ₹22.72 crore), PBT of ₹9.73 crore (up 46% from ₹6.65 crore) and net profit of ₹7.27 crore (up 44% from ₹5.04 crore). The Chairman said MS (formwork/scaffolding) volumes grew 7x YoY via temporary premises, while rental grew 24% and now contributes 46% of revenue. The company maintained an operating margin of about 40%, per the Chairman. Capacity remains the binding constraint: the Kosi Kotwan (Mathura) integrated plant targets operations by May 2027, and the formwork line is now targeted for December 2026 after machine delivery delays.

financial_highlights.change: +40% YoY vs ₹22.72 crore in Q1 FY26
Maintained despite inflation and growth investments

financial_highlights.metric: Margin by segment (as stated in Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: Rental about 47%; MS about 38%; aluminium about 10%
financial_highlights.change: Analyst reconciliation; management did not restate these as reported figures

financial_highlights.metric: Q1 expense on new plant/premises (as stated)
financial_highlights.value: ₹7.88 crore on new facility-related spend, later clarified as ₹8 crore
financial_highlights.change: Clarified as a continuous activity; the Q&A also cites ₹3.43 crore for the new plant

segments.name: Rental (scaffolding/access solutions)
segments.commentary: Rental grew 24% YoY and contributes 46% of revenue. Management said rental margins are higher and this is the company's main focus.

segments.name: MS (formwork/scaffolding) manufacturing
segments.commentary: MS volumes grew 7x YoY in Q1 by using temporary premises. Management expects MS share to rise, with formwork (aluminium) targeted for commercial production by December 2026.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork
segments.commentary: Four machines have arrived and are under operation, with five more pending; the company expects to complete installation by September 2026. Management said it is ready to trade at low margins if required.

guidance_outlook: IPO commitment of 50% CAGR reiterated by the Chairman; he said he could not confirm the exact figure cited in an interview.
Kosi Kotwan integrated manufacturing plant (Mathura) targeted to commence operations by May 2027; civil construction has begun.
New 500-ton-per-annum formwork/aluminium facility targeted to commence in December 2026, delayed from an earlier end-June target.
Management said the H1/H2 split for FY27 is roughly 40:60 for the new business, with the new formwork line not contributing materially in H1.
Chairman spoke of a ₹170 crore target and said the gap could be covered by all businesses; he did not provide a formal full-year target.
Initial formwork EBITDA margin may be lower than 20% during trials and ramp-up; no firm guidance given, and the 10-15% range was not confirmed.
capex_capacity: Kosi Kotwan (Mathura) integrated plant: 90 kg per annum augmentation (vs 30 kg already added via temporary premises), commissioning targeted May 2027.
Current MS capacity is almost fully utilised; management said it is at about 40% of its target peak, with peak utilisation of 80-90% expected after the new facility.
Management said the full ramp to 70-80% utilisation at the new facility would take about 6 months after commissioning.
A 30,000 sq m facility in Delhi (temporary premises) is in use; management is considering whether to vacate it after the new plant is running.
Capex: about ₹1 crore for machinery at the new plant, excluding land and civil works; ₹3-4 crore for certain assets was mentioned but not clearly attributed.
demand_pricing: Management said the company is currently about 10% of the Indian market for its products, and MS has not yet reached 10% share.
Competitive edge claimed: organised player, 21 warehouses across India, 24-hour delivery, and an ability to take orders from ₹5 crore upward. PSU orders also cited.
Aluminium market size cited as ₹1,300 crore currently, expected to reach ₹2,400 crore by 2030 (slide figure, as read out in the call).
Tubing is procured externally (no in-house extrusion); management plans an extrusion plant later.
Competitors' formwork EBITDA cited at about 20%; the company's own formwork margin not yet calculated, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue from the expanded capacity (25 kg and 90 kg), and why is the formwork expansion now ₹15 crore vs ₹4 crore earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the peak is not yet reached and the company is at about 40% of its target; the 25 kg/90 kg figures are capacity numbers, and the ₹15 crore figure is for robotic/automatic machines inclusive of rental. Steel and aluminium volumes were discussed in tonnes, not clearly reconciled to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any delay in the formwork timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Delivery of some machines was delayed; four have arrived and five are pending, and commercial production is now targeted for December 2026 versus an earlier end-June target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 50% CAGR target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chairman reiterated the IPO commitment of 50% CAGR but said he could not recall the specific figure quoted in an interview; he said the company hopes to achieve it.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new formwork business affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial margins may be lower due to trials and ramp-up; management expects them to normalise over time through scale and working-capital use. A 20% EBITDA margin was not confirmed; 10-15% was not confirmed either.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ₹170 crore target be achieved, given a delay in formwork?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chairman said all businesses would contribute and that the delay would be covered by other products; he did not give a segment-level breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ₹8 crore quarterly spend on the new facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spend is continuous through FY27 and could be more than ₹8 crore per quarter; the split between land, civil works and machinery was not provided.
